# iDiscovery Solutions

> iDiscovery Solutions (iDS) is a consulting firm of digital forensics, structured data, eDiscovery and damages experts who testify to their conclusions. Founded in 2008, with offices in Washington DC, Costa Mesa, Alpharetta and London.

## Key pages

- [iDiscovery Solutions | Digital Forensics & eDiscovery Experts](https://idsinc.com/): Digital forensics, structured data, and eDiscovery experts who defend their conclusions under oath. Know what your evidence shows before the other side does.
- [About iDiscovery Solutions: Experts Who Testify](https://idsinc.com/about/): iDS is a Chambers-ranked consultancy of digital forensics, eDiscovery, and data experts, founded in 2008, with offices in the US and London.
- [Capabilities: Nine Disciplines, One Evidentiary Foundation](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/): Digital forensics, structured data, eDiscovery, damages, investigations, cybersecurity, privacy, information governance, and expert testimony from one team.
- [Our Experts: Testifying Digital Forensics & Data Experts](https://idsinc.com/our-experts/): Meet the testifying experts and the bench behind iDS: digital forensics, structured data, damages, investigations, and cybersecurity, led by CEO Dan Regard.
- [Can You…? Questions Other Firms Declined to Answer](https://idsinc.com/can-you/): Generalized accounts of matters that began as questions other firms declined to answer, from class certification to trade secrets, and how iDS found the evidence.
- [AI & Evidence: Tech Enabled, Not Tech Dependent](https://idsinc.com/ai-evidence/): Where AI helps expert work, where it cannot replace judgment, and how iDS evaluates AI-generated evidence so conclusions hold up under cross-examination.
- [Contact iDS: Bring Us Your Question](https://idsinc.com/contact/): Tell us what you are trying to establish. The iDS team will say whether the evidence can get you there. Offices in Washington DC, California, Georgia, and London.
- [Careers at iDS: Expertise on an Expert-Built Platform](https://idsinc.com/careers/): A firm built by experts, for experts. Independently owned, with a 90-day launch program, growth coaching, and open roles in digital forensics and eDiscovery.

## Capabilities

- [Digital Forensics](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#digital-forensics): Your data tells a story: who created it, how, and when
- [Structured Data & Analytics](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#structured-data): Databases are evidence, and they behave differently
- [eDiscovery & Disclosure](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#ediscovery): A complete, defensible record, at a cost that is defensible too
- [Damages & Forensic Accounting](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#damages-forensic-accounting): Financial exposure, stated as a range with named assumptions
- [Investigations](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#special-investigations-unit): Rapid response when the incident carries legal risk
- [Cybersecurity](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#cybersecurity): A single incident can cause lasting organizational harm
- [Privacy](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#privacy): Rights requests are an evidence problem before they are a legal one
- [Information Governance & Compliance](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#information-governance): Reduce the risk before it becomes a matter
- [Expert Testimony](https://idsinc.com/capabilities/#testimony): The discipline every other discipline reports into

## Case studies

- [Investigating Inappropriate Access to a Company System](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/access-company-system/): iDS covertly analyzed 150 users within a week after an insider tip about improper access to payroll reports. No breach notification was required.
- [Capturing Data from 150 Mobile Devices in 48 Hours](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/capturing-data/): iDS built a forensic workflow that collected data from 150 mobile devices within a two-day window. Read the digital forensics case study.
- [Proving Copyright Infringement with Digital Evidence](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/copyright-infringement/): iDS testimony showed a copyright violator had been given proper takedown notices and ignored them. The client won at trial. Read the case study.
- [Coders Try to Outsmart Their Digital Footprints](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/digital-footprints/): In a software plagiarism suit, iDS traced the digital footprints two developers tried to hide. The court threw out the case and awarded fees to our client.
- [Custom Workflows Meet Every Disclosure Deadline](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/disclosure-obligations/): iDS collected 20 million records from 13 systems with custom workflows, and the client met every disclosure deadline. Read the eDiscovery case study.
- [Proof of a Doctored Text Message Wins Case](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/doctored-text-message/): iDS testimony showed the “text message” produced in a harassment claim was fabricated, and the client won at trial. Read the forensic case study.
- [Employees Gone Bad: Who Took What Data to a Competitor](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/employees-gone-bad/): iDS findings within one week supported a TRO, an injunction, and a favorable settlement after an ex-employee’s misappropriated pricing surfaced.
- [Working as a Forensic Neutral for Both Parties](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/forensic-neutral/): Retained by both parties as a neutral, iDS imaged phones and laptops to show how each side used its devices. The findings led to a confidential settlement.
- [Inappropriate Materials Result in Appropriate Termination](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/inappropriate-materials/): iDS testimony tied inappropriate viewing on a company computer to the employee’s account, and the client won a jury verdict in a wrongful termination suit.
- [Misappropriation of Trade Secrets: An Investigation](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/industry-trade-secrets/): An insurer that hired 70 employees from a competitor was accused of using trade secrets. iDS testimony showed no misappropriation, and the client won at trial.
- [LeanReview™ Isolates Key Documents for Interviews](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/leanreview/): LeanReview™ prioritized 2,225 documents out of 3 million, then 110 key documents, so counsel could prepare a week of employee interviews.
- [Structured Data Analysis Leads to Class Decertification](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/leveraging-structured-data/): iDS analyzed 75 billion records in a compensation class action, and the class was decertified six weeks before trial. Read the structured data case study.
- [Information Governance: The Playbook for Success](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/managing-information/): An information governance plan cut email retention from permanent to 18 months and reduced stored email by 75%. Read the iDS case study.
- [Data Shows an Employee Spent Half the Day Off-Task](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/non-work-activity/): iDS analysis proved half of an employee’s workday went to non-work activity, and the employee’s lawsuit was dropped. Read the investigation case study.
- [Produced Text Messages Were Hand-Selected and Incomplete](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/production-texts/): iDS showed the texts produced in litigation were hand-selected and the rest purged after filing, exposing screenshots that were not real threads.
- [Reasonable Security Measures in Protecting Trade Secrets](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/protecting-trade-secrets/): iDS evaluated a firm’s security program for trade secret protection. One opposing expert was withdrawn and the other conceded the security gaps.
- [User-Collected Data: Information Privacy Expertise](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/public-transportation/): iDS showed that a user-installed app is not a recording device, and a class action over alleged recording of transit passengers was dismissed.
- [Quick Recovery from a Ransomware Attack | iDS Case Study](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/quick-recovery-from-ransomware-attack/): Ransomware shut down a client’s headquarters. iDS restored operations within hours, protecting more than $1.5 million a day in revenue.
- [Internet Filtering Software: Reasonable Measures](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/reasonable-measures/): A school district was accused of exposing students to inappropriate sites. iDS showed filtering worked as designed and the activity was on a personal device.
- [Winning a Case with Just One Screenshot | iDS Case Study](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/screenshot-case/): iDS inspected an inoperable iPhone and a manipulated photo of texts. The court found the evidence false and awarded $158,000 in sanctions.
- [Video Surveillance Forensics: Collecting a Live System](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/surveillance-forensics/): iDS made a defensible collection of a live video surveillance system without taking it offline, for an overtime class action. Read the case study.
- [Suspected Data Breach: Was Reporting Necessary?](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/suspected-data-breach/): iDS found unauthorized access but no exfiltration, so little to no breach reporting was required. Read how the data was analyzed.
- [Insight into a Departed Employee’s User Activity](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/user-activity/): An iDS expert walked counsel through ERA™ results from a departed employee’s laptop within 48 hours, giving the case team assurance.
- [Defeating Overtime Class Certification with Video](https://idsinc.com/case-studies/video-analysis/): Years of security checkpoint footage showed alleged entry delays were exaggerated, and class certification in an overtime action was defeated.
